answer: The cheapest real defence: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because lantern only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, fable is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any walnut approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
